## Summary

Adds `ETag`, `Vary: Accept`, and `Cache-Control` headers to packument responses, and supports conditional requests (`If-None-Match`, `If-Modified-Since`) returning `304 Not Modified`.

Related to https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/131 (Section C10: Packument caching headers).

```text
responses, and return 304 Not Modified when an incoming If-None-Match or
If-Modified-Since header matches the current packument state.

- Compute strong ETag over rendered packument response body
- Return 304 Not Modified with empty body preserving ETag, Vary, and Cache-Control
- Support If-None-Match (with weak comparison per RFC 9110) taking precedence over If-Modified-Since
- Emit Vary: Accept on packument responses, preserving Accept and appending Authorization when private_no_cache applies
- Set Cache-Control: public, max-age={ttl} on public packuments from upstream maxage or config packument_ttl
- Maintain Cache-Control: private, no-store on private or caller-scoped responses
- Extract OSV filtering helpers into osv_filtering.rs and server lifecycle into lifecycle.rs to keep source files within line limits

Related to https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/131
```

fix(resolving): reject registry metadata that names another package
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

The npm resolver copied a packument's top-level `name` into the picked manifest without checking it against the requested package. A registry could answer a request for `@scope/a` with metadata naming `b`, and pnpm resolved it as `b@x`. Every name-keyed policy (`allowBuilds`, trust policy, `minimumReleaseAge` excludes) and the lockfile then saw `b`, not the package that was requested.

The GitHub Packages quirk keeps working. There the packument is `@owner/foo` and only the per-version manifest says `foo`, so the top-level name matches the request and the manifest name is pinned to it.

prs.title: docs: fix stale usage examples in six package READMEs
fix(fs-packlist): exclude npm-packlist's default ignore patterns from pack
prs.author: BerkayOzerSahin
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now leave out the files npm-packlist excludes by default. Before this change, pnpm 12 shipped them, while npm and pnpm 11 drop them:

- `.*.swp` (editor swap files, which can hold secrets)
- `._*` (macOS AppleDouble files and folders)
- `.lock-wscript`
- `.wafpickle-*`
- `build/config.gypi`
- `archived-packages/`
- the contents of a `.DS_Store` folder

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16955.

pnpm 11 is not affected: it delegates to npm-packlist 10.0.4, so this is a v12-only fix.

The rules match npm's semantics:

- **Applied in every directory.** `sub/build/config.gypi` and `lib/.lock-wscript` are excluded too.
- **Case-insensitive in ASCII**, like npm's matcher.
- **Overridable:**
  - a `files` entry naming the file, `main`/`bin`/`browser`, or a root `.npmignore` negation brings the file back;
  - `files: ["lib"]` still leaves out `lib/._a.js`, as npm does.

Real tarballs from the fixed binary match npm 11.19.1 in every scenario tested, including the issue's reproduction, nested anchored paths, `files` globs, named files, `main`/`bin`, workspace-inherited ignore files, and Unicode look-alike names.

**Known differences that predate this change** (not changed here, tracked as a follow-up):

- A `files` entry or a nested `main`/`bin` naming a file inside a default-excluded directory two or more levels deep: v12 ships it, npm drops it.
- npm skips its defaults at the root of a non-linked bundled dependency. v12 applies them there, which is stricter.

prs.title: fix(run): end an interrupted recursive run with the script's status
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

A single Ctrl+C during `pnpm -r --parallel run dev` or `pnpm --filter a run dev` on pnpm 12 printed `ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_FIRST_FAIL` and exited 1. With this change pnpm ends with the interrupted script's status (SIGINT, 130 in the shell) and prints no run failure, as pnpm 11 does since pnpm/pnpm#15209.

`run_stage` already left out the `[ELIFECYCLE]` line for a script the interrupt ended (pnpm/pnpm#16579). The recursive run still booked that script as a task failure, though. This PR carries the interrupted exit up to the run and ends with it through `exit_like`.

pnpm 11 is already fixed, so only the Rust CLI changes.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16964

## Squash Commit Body

```text
A Ctrl+C during a recursive or filtered `pnpm run` was booked as a task
failure. `run_stage` already skipped the `[ELIFECYCLE]` line for a script
the interrupt ended, but the recursive run still reported
`ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_FIRST_FAIL` and exited 1.

Track whether an interrupt reached pnpm while each script ran. A script
that then fails stops its task like a cancelled one, which stops further
dispatch. It does not cancel the siblings, which the same interrupt is
already shutting down. The run then ends through `exit_like` with that
script's status, so the shell sees SIGINT (130) as it does with pnpm 11.

Closes https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16964
```

prs.title: feat: split workspace settings across included files
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements the [config fragments RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/text/0000-config-fragments.md) in pnpm v12 (Rust only, per the v12/v11 policy), with one change to it: relative paths in an included file are measured from that file. That change is proposed to the RFC in pnpm/rfcs#40.

- **`include` in the root `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.** Each entry is a local `./`/`../` `.yaml`/`.yml` file or a declared config dependency. It maps to a list of settings or `'*'`; config dependencies always need a list. Catalogs are selected with `catalog`, `catalogs.<name>` or `catalogs`.
- **Relative paths in an included file are relative to that file**, the way paths in the root manifest are relative to the workspace root. This covers path settings, `packages` globs, `pnpmfile`, `patchedDependencies`, a `scriptShell` that contains a slash, and `file:`/`link:`/bare-path specifiers in catalogs and `overrides`. Absolute, `~` and `$VAR` paths are kept. - **One owner per setting.** A listed setting is reserved even when the file omits it. Conflicts fail with `ERR_PNPM_DUPLICATE_SETTING`, and an undelegated setting fails with `ERR_PNPM_SETTING_NOT_DELEGATED`. Legacy aliases share an owner with the setting t

prs.title: fix(gvs): keep the importer's parentURL on the resolve hook context
prs.author: maschwenk
prs.body:
## Summary

With `enableGlobalVirtualStore`, pnpm adds a resolve hook to `NODE_OPTIONS` that retries a failed bare specifier once per `NODE_PATH` entry with a synthetic parent such as `<root>/node_modules/x`. A resolve hook a script registers itself runs before pnpm's, and if it reads `context.parentURL` in its `catch` after pnpm's retries fail, it sees that synthetic parent rather than the importer. The tsconfig `paths` resolver in the issue then fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

Node.js keeps one context object for the whole hook chain and merges whatever a hook passes to `nextResolve` into it, for both `module.registerHooks()` and `module.register()`, so the `{ ...context, parentURL }` pnpm passes does not stay local to the retry.

The hook now saves `parentURL` before the retries and restores it in a `finally`, so earlier hooks see their own importer whether a retry succeeds or not. Both CLIs embed the same hook source, so the TypeScript package and the Rust copy change identically, in the sync and async variants, and the shared golden flag is regenerated.

The new test runs the issue's scenario in both stacks. Its alias hook falls back to `module.register()` where `registerHooks` is missing, so the Node.js 22.13 CI job covers the async variant. The test fails in both stacks with the fix reverted.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16979

prs.title: fix(pkg): normalize the repository field in pkg fix
prs.author: maschwenk
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm pkg fix` left `repository` as written, so `"repository": "github:pnpm/example"` stayed a shortcut. `npm pkg fix` rewrites it to `{ "type": "git", "url": "git+https://github.com/pnpm/example.git" }`, and the npm registry page shows no repository link for the shortcut form.

This ports the `fixRepositoryField` step of `@npmcli/package-json` to both CLIs:

- A non-empty `repository` string becomes `{ "type": "git", "url": <string> }`, `type` first.
- A `url` that hosted-git-info recognizes becomes `https()` for a shortcut, otherwise the form of its own protocol: `git+ssh://` for ssh and http, `git+https://` for https, and `git://` stays `git://` on GitHub.
- Unrecognized URLs, other keys such as `directory`, a non-string `url`, and values that are neither string nor object are left alone. A shortcut with no owner, such as `github:skills`, is left alone too. The legacy `repositories` array step is not ported.

The TypeScript CLI uses the hosted-git-info fork the git resolver already depends on. The Rust CLI adds `HostedGit::normalized_repository_url()`, because `HostedGit`'s `Display` renders the `git` and `http` forms differently from hosted-git-info's `toString()`.

Expected values in both test suites come from `npm pkg fix` (npm 11.19.0). One known difference: the Rust git host parser does not know gists, so `gist:abc123` is wrapped but its url is left as is, while the TypeScript CLI writes `git+https://gist.github.com/abc123.git` like npm.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#
…(truncated)

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Support the npm login web flow (`/-/v1/login`) so `npm login` and `pnpm login` authenticate via browser SSO when an OIDC login provider is configured (Related to https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/131).

- `POST /-/v1/login` and `POST /~{registry}/-/v1/login`: return `404 Not Found` if no OIDC provider has `login:` configured (allowing `npm login` / `pnpm login` to fall back to basic CouchDB auth); return `202 Accepted` with `loginUrl` and `doneUrl` and `Cache-Control: private, no-store` when enabled.

- `GET /-/v1/login/poll/{session}`: poll for granted CLI token; return `202 Accepted` with `Retry-After: 1` while pending, and `200 OK` with `{"token": "<token>"}` once authenticated, consuming the session.
- OIDC callback & sign-in: handle `return=cli&session={session}` and fulfill the CLI web login session upon completion with an informative confirmation page.
- Export `bundled_root_certs` in `pnpm-network` and configure reqwest client in `OidcState` with root certificates.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm deploy` (shared-lockfile mode) rejected every lockfile local path that resolved outside the lockfile directory, so a declared `file:../../client` dependency failed with `Refusing to deploy unsafe lockfile path`. Install links the same path, and pnpm v11 deploys it, so this is a v12-only regression.

The check guarded nothing: deploy only reads from these paths, and install already read them. The deploy target keeps its own validation. This PR drops the check and its error variant, and adds an e2e test that deploys a `file:` dependency outside the workspace. The test fails without the fix.

v11 is unaffected, so there is no v11 change.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16983

```text
links fine failed with "Refusing to deploy unsafe lockfile path". pnpm v11

already read them, so the check guarded nothing. The deploy target keeps
its own validation.
```

prs.title: fix(self-update): update the project pin under Homebrew or Corepack
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm self-update` refused to run under Homebrew or Corepack even in a project that pins pnpm, so the pin could not be bumped after `brew upgrade pnpm`. Now only the global switch is skipped under an external manager. The pin is updated and the command exits 0 with a note saying the global pnpm was left alone. Without a pnpm pin it still fails with `ERR_PNPM_CANT_SELF_UPDATE_IN_HOMEBREW` / `ERR_PNPM_CANT_SELF_UPDATE_IN_COREPACK`.

Fixed in both v12 (`pnpm/crates/cli/src/cli_args/self_update/externally_managed.rs`, dispatcher) and v11 (`pnpm11/engine/pm/commands/src/self-updater/selfUpdate.ts`), with the same messages.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17001

## Squash Commit Body

```text
`pnpm self-update` refused to run when Homebrew installed pnpm or
Corepack ran it, even in a project that pins pnpm. The refusal guards the
global switch, which would install a second pnpm shadowed by the one on
PATH. Writing the pin touches nothing Homebrew or Corepack manages.

Both CLIs now skip only the global switch under an external manager and
report it after the pin update. Without a pnpm pin the command still fails
with ERR_PNPM_CANT_SELF_UPDATE_IN_HOMEBREW / _IN_COREPACK.

In pnpm v12 the check stays in the dispatcher before config is loaded. It
now reads package.json from the same directory as the handler to decide
whether a pin exists.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17001
```

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm prune` hardcoded the lockfile policy to untrusted, so it ignored `trustLockfile` from every source and ran the supply-chain verification pass. That pass is what fetched registry metadata after "resolution step is skipped", so an offline prune with an empty metadata cache failed with `ERR_PNPM_META_FETCH_FAIL` / `ERR_PNPM_NO_OFFLINE_META`.

Prune now reads `config.trust_lockfile`, which `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `--config.trust-lockfile`, `pnpm_config_trust_lockfile`, and the bare `--trust-lockfile` / `--no-trust-lockfile` flags already set (the same path `pnpm update` uses).

pnpm v11 is not affected (the issue confirms prune works offline on 11.28.6), so this is v12-only.

Not changed:
- `pnpm prune --help` does not list `--trust-lockfile`, same as `pnpm update`. The flag works through the shared settings table.
- Without trust, a failing offline prune has already unlinked the pruned packages when it errors. Frozen installs run verification concurrently with fetch and link, so `pnpm install` behaves the same.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16999

fix(git-resolver): recognize the gist host
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

pnpm v12's `HostedGit` parser did not implement the gist host that hosted-git-info defines. The effects:

- `pnpm add gist:<id>` failed with a registry 404 on 12.13.0, while pnpm v11 installs it from the gist's archive.
- A gist URL was treated as an unknown host and kept verbatim.
- `pnpm pkg fix` left `"repository": "gist:abc123"` as written, while pnpm v11 and `npm pkg fix` write `git+https://gist.github.com/abc123.git` (follow-up from pnpm/pnpm#16981).

This adds a `Gist` host type that mirrors hosted-git-info's gist templates:

- Every URL form omits the owner: `gist:<id>`, `git+https://gist.github.com/<id>.git`, `git+ssh://git@gist.github.com/<id>.git`, `git://gist.github.com/<id>.git`.
- The archive is `https://codeload.github.com/gist/<id>/tar.gz/<commit>`, behind the same anonymous probe as the other hosts.
- The docs URL is `https://gist.github.com/<id>[/<commit>]`, as normalize-package-data writes it.
- The extractor rejects a `/<user>/<id>/raw/…` or `/<id>/raw/…` file URL and plain `http:`. Upstream reads the ownerless form as the gist `raw`.
- The name synthesized for a gist without a `package.json` is its id.

One deliberate deviation from upstream: the gist `https` and `git` forms keep URL-embedded credentials, as GitHub's do. Upstream drops them, which would strip the credentials from the URL `git ls-remote` reaches for a private gist. `pnpm pkg fix` still drops them from a gist `repository` url, as upstream does.

prs.title: feat(deps-restorer): let PNPM_MACOS_LINK_THREADS=0 link on the global pool
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to pnpm/pnpm#16906, as nilptr suggested in https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/16906#issuecomment-6207018414. `PNPM_MACOS_LINK_THREADS=0` now skips the dedicated link pool on macOS. Linking then runs on the calling thread's pool, which is the global rayon pool, as before pnpm/pnpm#16906.

That is the setting Macs with an Endpoint Security client need. On those Macs every file operation waits on the client, and only many calls in flight hide that wait. Before this change, the way to get there was `PNPM_MACOS_LINK_THREADS=16`, which runs 16 link threads on top of the 16 in the global pool.

### What changes

- `link_threads` returns `None` for `0`, and `in_link_pool` then builds no pool and runs the work on the calling thread's pool. Unset, negative or non-numeric values still mean 4.
- The settings page recommends comparing `0` with the default on Macs with such software.
- The unreleased changeset from pnpm/pnpm#16906 is amended to mention `0`, instead of adding a new one.

### Measurements

10-core M1 Max with an Endpoint Security client, macOS 27.0.1, 1352-package integrated-benchmark fixture, warm frozen install, hot store, isolated linker, GVS off. hyperfine, 10 runs each, two passes:

| `PNPM_MACOS_LINK_THREADS` | Pass 1 | Pass 2 |
|---|---|---|

prs.author: samanyudas
prs.body:
## Summary

close #17011

After a filtered install for one project, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` treated another selected project as up to date even when its dependencies had changed and were never installed. The script then ran without them, and `verifyDepsBeforeRun: error` and `warn` reported nothing.

**Root cause.** A filtered install writes one workspace-wide `lastValidatedTimestamp` while materializing only the projects it selected. For a later filtered command, the gate checks that each selected project has a modules directory and an importer in the current lockfile. Both hold for a project installed earlier. No manifest or lockfile is newer than the refreshed timestamp, so `check_freshness` returns early and never compares the current lockfile with the wanted one. The current lockfile still holds that project's importer from before the change.

**Fix.** When the state records a filtered install, the gate now also requires the current lockfile to record what the wanted lockfile materializes for the selection. It builds `materialization_closure` for the selected importers from both lockfiles and compares their importers, snapshots, and packages. Two details:

- The closures use the dependency groups the workspace state recorded. After `pnpm install --prod --filter …` the current lockfile has no dev dependencies, so comparing all groups would make the gate install before every script.
- Only the selected importers are compared. An unselected project that is still stale doe

## Summary

Adds a `defect-hotspots` agent skill. It finds the areas where fixes keep landing and fixes need follow-up fixes, then works from each loop to the design flaw behind it and the tests that would have caught it.

- `scripts/hotspots.mjs` collects the evidence:

- `implement-change` now asks a bug fix to check whether its code was fixed recently, and to fix the cause or say why this is another case of it.

The first run over 90 days of `main` found five loops. prs.author: zkochan

## Summary

Two changes to the official image workflow (`ghcr.io/pnpm/pnpm`).

**1. An Alpine variant.** This adds the `<version>-alpine`, `<major>-alpine`, and `alpine` tags for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. They're built from the musl release tarball.

The reporter in pnpm/pnpm#16973 installs pnpm into `node:*-alpine` with `curl https://get.pnpm.io/install.sh | sh`. Vercel's DDoS mitigation answers bursts of concurrent CI jobs with 403s. The existing image can't help there, because it ships the glibc build, which doesn't run on Alpine. With this change, Alpine users can build on the image or copy it into their own:

```dockerfile
FROM node:24-alpine
COPY --from=ghcr.io/pnpm/pnpm:12-alpine /opt/pnpm /opt/pnpm
RUN ln -s /opt/pnpm/pnpm /usr/local/bin/pnpm
```

The whole `/opt/pnpm` directory is copied, because `dist/` beside the binary holds the bundled node-gyp. The Alpine build runs only for releases with musl tarballs for both x64 and arm64, which means v12. v11 and v10 skip it.

**2. `latest` and `<major>` no longer move backwards.** Every release used to add these tags, so `ghcr.io/pnpm/pnpm:latest` points at 11.28.6 today. The builds now push only the exact version tags. A final step then moves `latest`/`alpine` only for the highest stable version overall, and `<major>`/`<major>-alpine` only for the highest version in that major, using `docker buildx imagetools create`.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements [pnpm/rfcs#39](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/pull/39), "zstd tarballs through tar integrity", in pnpm v12 and pnpr.

A registry can serve each package as the uncompressed tar of its `.tgz`, using HTTP content coding (zstd or gzip). Its metadata then pins the hash of the tar. Compression becomes a transport detail: no lockfile hash, signature, or provenance depends on the encoded bytes.

**pnpm v12**
- `serverType: pnpr` declares the `<registry>/<name>@<version>` layout, so lockfiles keep omitting tarball URLs.
- Tarball requests use HTTP clients that leave `Content-Encoding` in place. pnpm decodes the content coding itself, which is how it enforces the 8 MiB zstd window (RFC 9659): reqwest's built-in decoder allows 128 MiB and offers no setting. Metadata still goes through reqwest's decoder. Moving it is an open question in the RFC. The archive clients are built on the first archive request, so commands that download no archive do not pay for them.
- pnpm checks the first bytes of the decoded body: the gzip magic means a `.tgz`, anything else a tar. The hash covers the decoded resource either way.
- A decoded-output budget bounds the decoded tar before its hash is checked:
  - file payload: at most `maxTarballUnpackedSize` (new setting, 4 GiB), and for a tar also at most `dist.unpackedSize`;
  - headers and skipped entries: at most 256 MiB;
  - after the end-of-archive marker: at most 10 KiB of zeros;
  - an empty body fails the package.

**`lockfile.integrityTarget: tar` (pnpm v12)**
- With the setting on, every package tarball entry in `pnpm-lock.yaml` (registry packages, `tarball:` URLs, `file:` tarballs) pins the hash of its uncompressed tar. The lockfile records this as `settings.integrityTarget: tar`.
